source.title: RepIt: Steering Language Models with Concept-Specific Refusal Vectors
source.authors: Vincent Siu; Nathan W. Henry; Nicholas Crispino; Yang Liu; D. Song; Chen-Guang Wang

record.file_problem: The text is cut off during Appendix E, in the example responses section. The main paper and substantial appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study intervenes on difference-in-means-derived directions and reports refusal-related outcomes, but its results also argue that multiple representational pathways can produce the targeted behavior. It presents concept-specific, partially orthogonalized vectors rather than testing the original all-layer, all-position ablation and addition recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper reports behavioural outcomes for RepIt and unmodified DIM steering, plus component-direction comparisons. Direction and hyperparameter values used only for selection, and results cited from other work, are not recorded as rows. Figure-only values are left as figure only; the text gives only aggregate ranges or qualitative descriptions for many plotted results.
record.test_reason: The study steers refusal with single-layer ACE using difference-in-means vectors across five models, two kinds of vector in particular. First, raw DIM vectors (target WMD, mean non-target, and the shared projection αP) each jailbreak WMD prompts; this bears on V1 and on V8 for the reasoning checkpoints. Second, a partially orthogonalized concept-specific residual (RepIt) removes WMD refusal while other refusal stays near baseline; the authors use this to argue refusal must be restated as entangled, multi-pathway structure (V4). It is mainly a method paper, but these results bear on the versions. It is not the original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also stress three points. Target ASR reaches up to 0.7 with non-target increases around 0.1. Concept vectors can be built from about 12 prompts, and the edit localizes to 100–200 dimensions. Concept-matched benchmarks (HarmBench) underestimate harm, so representation-aware auditing is needed. They link the multi-pathway finding to concept cones.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-category-minus-Alpaca DIM vectors, then reweights, whitens, and partially orthogonalizes against non-target DIM vectors. COSMIC selects a layer and position; ACE intervenes there across tokens. This differs from ablating one direction at every layer and position, and does not test adding the direction to induce harmless refusal.
record.method_sensitivity: The selected ρ and resulting vector vary by model and target category. The paper reports different degrees of entanglement across model sizes and categories; the ρ search is performed at a COSMIC-selected layer and position. Reasoning models use a 1500-token generation limit versus 500 for non-reasoning models.

fits_no_version.finding: PCA of the 21 non-target DIM vectors: the first ~10 principal components explain over 90% of variance in all five models (Appendix C.1, Fig 9). This is geometry with no behavioural rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Category-wise refusal DIM vectors share a compact low-rank (~10-dim) subspace rather than a single direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparsifying the RepIt edit to 96–213 heavy-tail coordinates leaves ASR within ±0.05 (Table 1), with several percent of prompts flipping each way (Table 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The concept-specific correction to a refusal DIM vector is concentrated in a few residual-stream coordinates.

record.problems: The text notes semantic ambiguity and category overlap, imperfect disentanglement, and that untested concepts may remain entangled. Main figure values are not provided numerically in the text. ASR is judged by LlamaGuard 3 and does not establish that outputs contain actionable or factual harmful information. No general-capability benchmark is reported. Exact WMD prompts are not yet publicly available, and the paper says full reproducibility awaits controlled data release.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix Figure 4 data-size sweeps, Table 1 sparse-projection ΔASR results, Table 6 tailweighting prompt flips, Figures 6–10, and other ablations are not included. They report additional RepIt variants, data-efficiency or diagnostic analyses, but were omitted to keep rows focused on the core direction intervention, its refusal outcomes, and the component evidence for V4.

untested.parts: No addition of the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts; no all-layer/all-position ablation (single COSMIC-selected layer with ACE); no general-capability benchmark; no broad harmful-minus-harmless direction (category-specific DIMs only).
Not tested: no weight edit was made, released or verified; the paper only states ACE is equivalent to a static weight edit.
No addition, all-layer ablation, capability or reasoning-trace analysis for the reasoning models; only single-layer DIM removal with target ASR, and values are figure-only.

missing.what: Non-target ASR (JailbreakV, StrongREJECT, TDC2023, JailbreakBench, AdvBench, MaliciousInstruct) under the unmodified WMD DIM vector, per model. The text says spillover is larger in GLM-4.1V/Mistral and smaller in 4B models.
LlamaNemo4B DIM vectors already concept-specific: ρ=0 for Chem/Cyber, cosine 1.00 between RepIt and raw vectors. Cosine is 0.59–0.81 for GLM/Mistral.
Toxicity (ToxiGen) target experiment. RepIt and DIM target and non-target ASR; DIM in LlamaNemo4B and Phi4-mini is nearly orthogonal to other refusal concepts, with minimal spillover.
Per-category (Bio/Chem/Cyber) and per-model ASR for the vt, R, αP and vRepIt vectors; rows r41–r44 are only aggregates.

record.verdict_notes: The ACE intervention itself is the affine refusal edit of Marshall et al. It is applied at one COSMIC-selected layer, so no row tests V1's all-layer recipe or addition. The authors' 'multiple pathways' reading of r41/r42 is weak: non-target and shared-projection vectors jailbreaking the target fits a shared dominant direction (V1). The V4-relevant evidence is the concept-specific residual that selectively removes refusal. ASR is judged by LlamaGuard 3 only, with no capability checks. All per-model values are figure-only. Reasoning models used a 1500-token limit versus 500 for the others.

versions.untested_parts: No addition intervention that induces refusal on harmless prompts; no ablation of one direction at every layer and position; no broad general-capability evaluation. RepIt uses target-category DIM vectors, orthogonalization, and steering at a selected layer and position.

The paper describes its ACE intervention as equivalent to a static weight edit, but does not report a separate conversion, release, or verification of edited weight files. It does not show complete removal of all refusal.
The study does not test whether other attacks work by suppressing the original refusal direction, or whether training against that ablation improves robustness.
The results support multiple pathways for the tested concept-steering effects; they do not comprehensively compare affine, cone, and dominant-direction models of refusal.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment versus refusal decision.
Models are tested individually; the paper does not transfer a direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct checkpoints.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages for whether a removable direction emerges.
The paper tests targeted steering in reasoning models, not the full original all-layer/all-position ablation and addition claim, nor a broad capability battery for reasoning models.

relationships.condition: Single-layer ACE removal with raw DIM vectors (target WMD vt, mean non-target R, shared projection αP) on WMD prompts across five models
relationships.reason: Each DIM-derived vector jailbreaks WMD prompts, and the text says DIM achieves much higher ASR than RepIt (r36–r43). Values are figure-only.
relationships.display_finding: Each tested difference-in-means-derived vector enabled WMD jailbreaks, with ASR reported as much higher than RepIt.

relationships.condition: Category-specific DIM vectors in 4B models, especially LlamaNemo4B
relationships.reason: From text, not rows: WMD-derived DIM vectors spread less to other harmful datasets in 4B models, and LlamaNemo4B's are already concept-specific (ρ=0, cos 1.00). So one WMD direction does not remove refusal broadly there.
relationships.display_finding: WMD-derived directions transferred less across harmful datasets in 4B models, with LlamaNemo4B already showing concept specificity at ρ=0 and cosine similarity 1.00.

relationships.condition: RepIt residual vectors on five models, WMD target vs JailbreakV/StrongREJECT and four unseen benchmarks

relationships.display_finding: The concept-specific residual removed WMD refusal at rates of 0.4–0.7 while other refusal stayed near baseline, with steering strength selected to keep non-target ASR below 0.1.

relationships.condition: Strength of the concept-specific component relative to the shared component

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Strength of the concept-specific component relative to the shared component
